name: Wollongong CBD
tagline: The centre, the station and the shortest walk to the beach
description: The commercial core around Crown Street, with the mall, the station, most of the coworking and the highest concentration of apartments in the city. The beach is a ten-minute walk east and the train to Sydney leaves from here, which is the practical argument for the area.
bestFor: Anyone commuting to Sydney occasionally or working without a car
pros: Train to Sydney from the doorstep
Apartments with the best internet in the city
cons: Quiet and a little bleak on weekends
Some blocks feel rough late at night

name: North Wollongong
tagline: Beach, pubs and the university crowd
description: The strip between the CBD and North Beach, with the North Gong Hotel, the surf club and a run of cafes along the coastal path. It is the liveliest part of the city on a warm evening and where most of the beach-facing rental stock sits.
bestFor: Swimmers, surfers and anyone who wants the sea two minutes away
pros: Directly on the best city beach
The most active bar and cafe strip
Coastal shared path runs through it
cons: The most expensive rents in the city
Loud on weekends near the pubs
Parking impossible on a hot Saturday

name: Keiraville and Gwynneville
description: The residential streets around the University of Wollongong, rising towards the escarpment with the botanic garden between them and the city. Student share houses set the rental market, which makes it cheaper than the beach, and the bushwalks up Mount Keira start at the top of the hill.
bestFor: Cheaper long stays with the escarpment trails at the door
pros: Rents well below the beachside suburbs
Botanic garden and escarpment walks nearby
Free shuttle bus to the university and the city
cons: Student turnover makes leases short and noisy
Twenty-five minutes on foot to the beach

name: Thirroul
tagline: The northern beach village on the train line
description: A village fifteen minutes north by train, with a good beach, a rock pool, a bookshop and a cafe strip that has drawn people out of Sydney for years. D H Lawrence wrote Kangaroo here in 1922. It is the prettiest place to live on this coast and priced accordingly.
bestFor: People who want the escarpment and the beach and will pay for it
pros: Direct train to both Wollongong and Sydney
Excellent cafes and a strong village feel
Escarpment trails and beach both minutes away
cons: Fifteen minutes from the city for anything larger

name: Port Kembla
tagline: The industrial south, cheap and changing
description: The suburb around the steelworks and the port at the southern end of the city, historically working class and migrant, with the cheapest rents in the area and a wide beach that most visitors never reach. Wentworth Street has slowly picked up a few good places.
bestFor: Budget stays where price outweighs everything else
pros: The cheapest rents anywhere in the city
A genuinely good and uncrowded beach
Strong Macedonian and Italian food heritage
cons: The steelworks dominates the outlook and the air
Reputation and crime rates worse than the north
